content.comment_body: Hello! I'm experienced with PLCs, but new to the [product_name] series. I'm enjoying moving away from ladder diagrams and finding the function block diagram and simulation helpful. I'm confused about the buttons on the panel of the logic module ([product_name], [article_no]). No matter what I try, I can't figure out how to use them as intended. Does anyone know how to make the program respond directly to the cursor keys? Right now, I have to hold the ESC key for program blocks to react, and I can only get it to work by pressing ESC with C1-4. Also, is there a way to hide the menus from the user? I want the user to only see a simple main screen; accidental menu navigation could cause confusion. I'm feeling out of my depth with this. Any advice would be great! Thanks. [user_name]

Hi, Unfortunately, that's how [product_name] operates. You need to use the ESC button along with the cursor keys. There's no way to block the menus. You can hide parameter settings by adjusting protection for a block, such as for a timer. If you need a more user-friendly experience, consider using a [product_name] operator device. There, you can define your own menu on the F1–F4 keys and set custom options. For examples, see Menu control with [product_name] operator device at: Application examples for [product_name]. Regards,

Thanks for the explanation! I'd definitely appreciate more customization options and the ability to set variables. I'm not used to programming without any variables (besides flags and counters). The [product_name] is decent, but nearly too basic for my current project. I do have an operator device, so I'll try using that. Should work for my needs. Regards, [user_name]
Hello, The [product_name] is designed for small-scale applications, but with some ingenuity, you can do quite a bit. You can simulate a variable using a mathematical instruction. Regards,

Yes, it's more flexible than I initially thought. Took me some time to adjust my approach. We're slightly off-topic, but you mention creating a variable via mathematical instructions. I understand I can store a mathematical result in an analog flag. How could I set up a variable to store the machine's current 'mode'? For example, sometimes I may need to store the value '3', or later '26'. Is there a way to implement something like: mode = 3 or mode = 26? For the current issue, I managed by setting up latching relays: If input I2 equals X, then set latching relay 3. Later: If latching relay 3 is set, then execute an action. I feel more confident programming microcontrollers, so this is a bit different for me. Regards, [user_name]
Hello, You might use the analog multiplexer to pick your variable and then trigger actions with an analog threshold. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Users moving from other PLCs to the [product_name] platform appreciate features such as function block diagram programming and built-in simulation. However, they find the interface for front panel inputs restrictive, as direct use of cursor keys in custom programs requires holding the ESC key and cannot be reconfigured. There are usability concerns due to the inability to hide or restrict system menus, which can make navigation confusing for end-users. Variable handling is seen as less straightforward, primarily relying on analog flags and relay mechanisms rather than more standard approaches from other PLC environments.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to interact with their program using the cursor keys without needing to press ESC, and want options to hide or restrict system menus so only tailored screens are visible to end-users.
